title: Adaptive Degradation Safety & Verification Manual
author: Sanjay Rao
body:
Summary:

This manual defines the safety contracts, verification checks, benchmarking protocols, and operational runbooks we use to validate adaptive degradation and fallback behavior in the Redwood serving runtime. It is intended for runtime engineers, SREs, and release owners who gate runtime and scheduler changes. The document consolidates architecture contracts, test harnesses, profiling playbooks, measurable acceptance criteria, and incident response steps into a single reference.

Scope:
- Covers adaptive degradation (fidelity staircases, model-variant fallback, burst shedding) and scheduler/kernel interactions.
- Includes verification checks executed in CI, pre-release staging, and canary phases.
- Prescribes profiling and benchmark procedures for SLO verification and performance regressions.
- Provides runbooks for on-call and release owners for graceful rollback and mitigation.

Principles and safety goals:
1) Observable and measurable: every degradation path must have a minimal observable signal (metrics, traces, events) and a single source-of-truth trace ID for forensic replay.
2) Fail open vs fail closed rationale: correctness-critical requests (enterprise-configured) should prefer fail-closed; non-critical/latency-sensitive requests can fail open to preserved throughput.
3) Bounded fidelity loss: fidelity steps should degrade quality predictably (quantified by eval sets) and be reversible.
4) Deterministic rollback: any automated fallback must expose a deterministic rollback path and human-confirmable guardrails.

Architecture contracts (high-level):
- Degradation tiers: primary (full model), degraded-1 (quantized), degraded-2 (short-context variant), fallback (smaller model / cached-embeddings). Each tier has an SLO budget and cost profile.
- Kernel scheduling contract: the scheduler must maintain per-request kernel affinity for the first N tokens and preserve KV cache affinity during tier transition windows (default N=16).
- Eviction and warmup contract: when a session is evicted from KV cache, a warmup window of configurable length (default 60s) is reserved to rehydrate frequently-seen prompts without degrading SLOs.

Verification matrix (summary table):
| Check ID | Purpose | Where executed | Acceptance threshold | Action on fail | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| VD-01 | End-to-end tail latency under 95th percentile SLO | CI staging + canary | p95 < 1200ms for interactive path | block release, auto-rollback in canary | runtime-sre |
| VD-02 | Kernel latency jitter for hot kernels | perf-lab | 95th/50th ratio < 3.0 | schedule throttling + revert kernel flags | runtime-kernel-team |
| VD-03 | Fidelity regression on golden prompt set | automated evals | task-specific metric delta < 1.5% | fail gating | applied-ml |
| VD-04 | KV cache hitrate during warmup | synthetic replay | hitrate > 70% after 120s | degrade to cached-response fallback | runtime-sre |
| VD-05 | Correctness of fallback routing (no request loss) | chaos lab | 0 dropped requests during routing switch | incident | runtime-oncall |

Verifiable artifacts for each check:
- Synthetic replay corpus snapshot (sha256) used in CI.
- Expected telemetry schemas (metric names, tags) and trace samples.
- Baseline benchmark outputs (binary artifacts) for diff-based gating.

CI and pre-release harnesses:
1) CI unit stage: microbenchmarks for individual kernels (latency, occupancy, memory). Thresholds are enforced as fast-fail rules.
2) Staging perf run: full-stack replay of production traffic sampled (1:1000) with degraded-tier injection. Output artifacts: histogram dumps, kernel traces, KV cache heatmaps.
3) Canary: traffic ramp with A/B model variants and automated rollback on VD-* failures. Canary policy: 1% -> 5% -> 20% over 30m windows with automated health checks every 5m.

Benchmarking protocol (detailed):
- Workloads to run:
  - Interactive short-chat (mean tokens=40, 90th=128) — target low-latency SLOs.
  - Streaming long-output (mean tokens=800) — target throughput and memory stability.
  - Embeddings burst (large batch sizes) — target batching efficiency and memory footprint.
- Metrics collected:
  - end_to_end_latency_ms (p50/p90/p95/p99), kernel_exec_time_ms per-kernel, gpu_mem_used_mb, kv_cache_hitrate_pct, tokens_per_second_per_gpu.
- Tooling & commands (examples):
  - Run synthetic replay: 
    ./perf-runner --profile=replay --corpus=sha256:abcd1234 --duration=15m --out=artifacts/replay-$(date +%s).tgz
  - Microbenchmark kernel: 
    python tools/microbench.py --kernel matmul --batch 1 --seq 128 --out json --repeat 50
  - Collect trace samples for a request: 
    curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $CI_TOKEN" https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"<<golden>>"}' -o /tmp/trace.json
- Acceptance criteria pattern:
  - No p95 regression > 8% vs baseline.
  - Kernel jitter (95/50) <= 3.0.
  - KV cache delta < 5% hitrate loss after warmup period.

Profiling playbook snippets (how-to):
1) Latency fingerprint collection (on perf-lab machine):
  - Start full instrumentation: export PERF_SAMPLER=on; ./runtime --enable-tracing --trace-sample-rate=0.01
  - Run workload for 10 minutes and collect traces: tar -czf traces.tgz /var/tmp/traces/*
  - Post-process: python tools/trace-aggregate.py --input traces.tgz --output traces-summary.json
2) Kernel causality mapping:
  - Use kernel-hint exporter to annotate kernels with request-id and token-index. Example PromQL to find kernel hotpaths: sum(rate(kernel_exec_time_ms_bucket[5m])) by (kernel_name)
3) Latency attribution checklist:
  - Confirm p95 skew aligns with a specific kernel or queue time via trace waterfall.
  - Check GPU utilization and eviction events within the window.
  - Validate KV cache hit/miss correlation with session affinity changes.

Runbook: Adaptive Degradation incident triage (short):
1) Detection: Alert triggers if p95 or error-rate breaches gating thresholds (see Verification matrix).
2) Initial triage (first 10 min):
  - Owner: oncall-runtime.
  - Query: run the baseline PromQL dashboards (listed below) and capture current vs baseline.
  - Commands:
    - promql: rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m]) by (route)
    - runtime CLI: runtimectl list-sessions --filter=evicted=true --since=10m
3) Containment (10–30 min):
  - If caused by kernel regression: flip kernel rollout gate to previous stable tag (runtimectl kernel-set active:stable-<tag>) and pause canaries.
  - If caused by cache warmup regression: enable elevated pre-warm (config: prewarm_multiplier=2) and route new sessions to degraded-1 temporarily.
4) Remediation (30–90 min):
  - Roll back flagged config or kernel. Run perf-runner quick replay to validate.
  - If degradation persists, scale dedicated pool capacity for 15 minutes to reduce pressure and collect artifacts.
5) Post-incident verification: Ensure all VD-* checks pass in staging before re-enabling automated rollouts.

Release gating checklist (for runtime and scheduler changes):
- Code owner review and ADR reference.
- Automated CI checks: unit tests, lint, kernel microbenchmarks.
- Perf artifacts present: replay corpus, baseline histograms, and guard thresholds.
- Canary policy configured and health checks defined (list health checks and thresholds attached).
- Rollback plan and human approvers designated in the release ticket.

Instrumentation and metrics schema (quick reference):
- metric names: runtime.request.latency_ms, runtime.kernel.exec_ms, runtime.kv.hits, runtime.fidelity.tier, runtime.eviction.count
- required tags: service, model_name, model_variant, route, region, canary_id
- recommended tracing fields: request_id, session_id, token_index, kernel_name, warmup_phase

Ownership and escalation:
- Runtime architecture owner: runtime-arch@redwood.ai (primary: Sanjay Rao).
- Kernel scheduling owner: kernel-team@redwood.ai.
- Oncall rota: runtime-sre (see internal roster).
- Escalation path: oncall -> SRE lead -> runtime-arch -> Eng Director (timed escalation at 45m).

Appendices:
A) YAML example: adaptive degradation policy (example config to be applied via runtime fleet config)

  degradation_policy:
    tiers:
      - name: primary
        model_variant: v2-full
        slos:
          p95_latency_ms: 900
      - name: degraded-1
        model_variant: v2-quantized
        slos:
          p95_latency_ms: 700
      - name: degraded-2
        model_variant: v2-shortctx
        slos:
          p95_latency_ms: 350
    warmup:
      kv_cache_warmup_seconds: 120
      prewarm_multiplier: 1.5
    fallback:
      strategy: route-to-smaller-model
      max_inflight_fallback: 250

B) PromQL examples (quick):
- p95 latency for route: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(runtime_request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
- kernel jitter index: (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(kernel_exec_time_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, kernel)))/(histogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(kernel_exec_time_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, kernel)))

C) Minimal reproduction recipe for regressions:
1) Snapshot failing commit and baseline artifacts.
2) Run perf-runner with the failing kernel flag enabled and the baseline corpus.
3) Collect traces (traces.tgz) and microbench outputs.
4) Upload artifacts to /artifacts/regressions/<ticket-id>.

Related reading and references:
- See routing and fallback architecture ADR (link in related_pages).
- Profiling playbooks and telemetry contract (links in related_pages).

Notes and change log:
- 2026-01-15: Initial draft and adoption of verification matrix (S. Rao).
- 2026-03-10: Added canary ramp policy and refined kernel warmup contract; added runbook remediation steps (E. Hart, D. Alvarez).

If you are implementing a new scheduler or kernel change, follow this manual start-to-finish: 1) add microbench checks, 2) register threshold baselines, 3) run staging replay, 4) validate VD-* checks, 5) enable canary with the configured ramp, 6) monitor and be ready to rollback.
